description: Closed, versioned registry of learning event types. The event_type enum in learning-event.schema.json mirrors this registry and is the machine-enforced gate; unregistered event types are rejected by Core. DLC, Agents and Providers can never invent event names or write events directly. Adding or changing an event type requires an ADR, a learning-event schema version bump, and Human approval. Chat-mode activity never enters this event stream.

event_types.description: A LearningSession passed the three-layer readiness gate (Core ready, valid DLC, valid MaterialSnapshot, compiled IR, entitlement, Provider capabilities or explicit fallback) and execution started.
The session reached a normal stop primitive with a typed success result.

The session ended abnormally with a typed abort_reason (material_unavailable, provider_unavailable, budget_exhausted, timeout, dlc_compile_failed, hard_stop, learner_exit, entitlement_lost). No half-written state may remain.
The executor presented an activity lowered from DLC-declared high-level training modes into closed runtime primitives.
The learner submitted a response. Raw text/audio/large objects are stored as artifact references, never inline arbitrary JSON.

An evaluator produced a typed observation (binary/scalar/rubric_vector/timed/artifact_evidence/abstention). performance and measurement_confidence are strictly separated; not yet accepted as evidence.

An observation passed schema, permission, provenance, evaluator and measurement-confidence gates and now counts as evidence for or against one claim. Independence is deduplicated by evidence_group_id; duplicate idempotency keys never increase evidence counts.

The Core policy interpreter produced a MasteryDecision (not_yet/provisional/learned/uncertain/lapsed) under a specific evidence policy version. Revocable; policy upgrades create new decisions, never rewrite old ones.
A delayed retest or review was scheduled by the rule_based scheduler or a DLC-selected memory scheduler (e.g. fsrs_memory). Memory schedulers may only schedule; they never declare learned.
Structured feedback was presented to the learner. Raw pronunciation scores are never exposed directly; feedback follows the evidence-centered report protocol.
The learner accepted or acknowledged a correction. Acceptance is an event fact, not by itself evidence of mastery.
The session composition (core_version/dlc_ref/material_snapshot_ref/learning_ir_ref) was upgraded mid-session; the new composition is recorded and subsequent events reference it.
A human correction was appended as an event. Projections are never edited directly; manual corrections only enter state through appended events.

A LearnerStateProjection was deterministically rebuilt from the event stream. The payload reference records reducer/projector id, version, event sequence boundaries and input hash. Same event stream + same versions = field-identical projection.
